title: Stop a clean relaunch warning about a session that isn't running, and name the branch on a fresh repository

history.detail:
FAIL: QA1 gate-1 audit, sprint 38, round 1. Audited commit b49fbcf (on e573e96, the sprint start). The sprint file was read fresh at HEAD and is unchanged since e573e96. Verdict: FAIL. Two demonstrated defects, both the same shape: a check that could not actually run is reported as a definite answer. Both fixes are small. All defects are listed here so there is one fix round.

1. [HIGH] Req 1a: isPidAlive() returns false ("positively confirmed gone") when ps is present but cannot answer, which silences the NOTE for a session that is still running.
 - Code (scripts/launcher/role-claims.js, isPidAlive): after process.kill(pid, 0) has already SUCCEEDED, i.e. the process exists, it runs ps -o stat= -p <pid> and does "if (ps.status !== 0 || !stat) return false; // gone by the time ps checked". A ps that exits non-zero for any reason other than the pid being gone is read as "gone".
 - Real-world trigger, shown directly: BusyBox ps (Alpine, and many slim containers and devcontainers) does not support -p. In a real alpine container, docker run --rm --entrypoint sh public.ecr.aws/supabase/vector:0.53.0-alpine -c 'sleep 30 & P=$!; ps -o stat= -p $P; echo exit=$?' prints BusyBox usage text and "ps exit=1 for live pid 7".
 - End-to-end repro of the real code at b49fbcf (macOS). A PATH shim ps reproduces BusyBox's behaviour (usage on stderr, exit 1). Spawn a real sleep 30, then:
   - process.kill(pid,0) says running: true.
   - isPidAlive(pid) returns false.
   - roleClaimWarning('Master Controller', {pid}) returns null, so no NOTE is printed for a previous session that is demonstrably still running.
 - This is exactly the dangerous direction Sprint 25 and Req 1a exist to prevent: "a check that cannot be performed on this platform ... the NOTE fires as it does today", and the acceptance criterion says "every undeterminable branch falls through to the NOTE".
 - Fix: when kill(pid,0) succeeded but ps did not return a usable STAT, do not return false. Re-probe kill(pid,0): ESRCH means false (genuinely gone in between); anything else means null. Add a launcher_test case with a PATH-shimmed failing ps against a live process asserting the NOTE still fires.

2. [MEDIUM] Req 2: branch_state() reports "(not a git repository)" for a real repository whenever git refuses to run.
 - Code (scripts/sprint_lifecycle.py, branch_state): "if repo_check.returncode != 0 or repo_check.stdout.strip() != 'true': return ('no-repo', None)". Every non-zero exit from git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree becomes the specific claim "not a git repository".
 - Req 2 says the undeterminable cases "must not claim any of the three specific cases above".
 - Repro at b49fbcf, in a real clone (.git present, git log works): GIT_TEST_ASSUME_DIFFERENT_OWNER=1 (git's own hook for its safe.directory ownership check). git rev-parse --is-inside-work-tree then exits 128 with "fatal: detected dubious ownership in repository at ...", and branch_state() returns ('no-repo', None), so tree_description() prints ".../s38 (not a git repository)".
 - Real trigger: a repository owned by a different OS user than the one running git. That is common on Windows (created elevated, or on a VM shared folder), which is one of this sprint's two workshop platforms. An attendee would be told their repo isn't a repo, and told to run git init in a directory that already has one.
 - Fix: only claim "no-repo" when git positively says so (stderr "not a git repository", or exit 0 with stdout "false" for a non-work-tree). Treat any other failure as ("unknown", None). Add a smoke case using GIT_TEST_ASSUME_DIFFERENT_OWNER=1 asserting the output does NOT say "not a git repository".

WHAT IS FINE.
 - Req 1: the claim records the launcher's own pid (process.pid). run-role.js awaits spawnClaude for the whole session, so the launcher pid is alive exactly as long as the session. It is recorded before the fail() preflight paths, so a launcher that fails early leaves a dead pid, which is correct.
 - Suppression happens only on an exact === false. A missing or invalid pid returns null, so the NOTE fires. EPERM returns true. Both are correct.
 - On Dev Team's zombie question: the approach is sound. kill(pid,0) cannot see a zombie, and ps STAT Z is the right discriminator on POSIX. The only defect is the failure fallthrough in item 1.
 - On the pty-close measurement: a real pty.fork with the master closed is a faithful reproduction of a terminal disposing its pty (process-group SIGHUP reaching both processes), and it is measured, not argued. It is a stand-in for VS Code's trash can, not VS Code itself; LiveQA's live criteria cover the real thing.
 - The targeted-SIGKILL residual is named honestly.
 - 1c: an old-format record (no pid) returns null, so the NOTE fires. Tested.
 - A grep of the diff for "nobody else"/"nobody is working" finds no such output or comment; the existing NOTE wording is unchanged.
 - Req 2: symbolic-ref --short HEAD resolves an unborn branch and fails on a detached HEAD, which then correctly falls to unknown. Every tree_description() call site gets the new text; nothing is special-cased. The stderr [sprint_lifecycle] banner is untouched (no banner lines in the diff). current_branch() has no remaining callers.
 - Smoke asserts printed text for no-repo, unborn (a real git init with no commits), named, and detached.
 - Req 3: npm view fully-completely version returns 0.2.11 and package.json is 0.2.12; the CHANGELOG entry is present and accurate.
 - Req 4: QA1 ran both suites at b49fbcf in a clean clone. node scripts/launcher_test.js: ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED, exit 0. bash scripts/smoke_test.sh: ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED, exit 0. pyflakes is clean.
 - Diff confinement: exactly role-claims.js, sprint_lifecycle.py, launcher_test.js, smoke_test.sh, package.json and CHANGELOG.md, all on the allowed list; run-role.js is untouched, correctly.

FOR LIVEQA, not a finding here. Windows is unmeasured in this build, and run-role.js's own orphan-guard comment says the guard is POSIX-only and claude runs as a grandchild of cmd.exe on Windows. If a Windows trash-can or Terminate All ever kills the node launcher but leaves claude running, the recorded pid reads as gone and the NOTE is suppressed while a session is live. The F6 report's Get-Process observation suggests claude does die on that path, but LiveQA's per-step Get-Process check is what actually settles it. Check claude's state, not only the launcher's.

REQUIRED BEFORE PASS: fix items 1 and 2, each with a test that fails on b49fbcf.

PASS: QA1 gate-1 audit, sprint 38, round 2. Audited commit a21fcbd (HEAD). The sprint file was re-read and is byte-identical to e573e96, so the requirements have not moved. This round reviews b49fbcf..a21fcbd against the two round-1 findings, on top of the round-1 review of everything else. Verdict: PASS.

1. isPidAlive and an unusable ps (HIGH): FIXED, and demonstrated fixed.
 - Every ps failure path (a throw, ps.error, or a non-zero exit or empty STAT) now goes through reprobeAfterUnusablePs(). That re-runs process.kill(pid, 0) and returns false only on a fresh ESRCH, null otherwise. A genuine exit in the window between the two probes still reads as gone; a ps that cannot answer never does.
 - The zombie path (STAT starting with Z means false) is unchanged.
 - QA1's own repro, re-run at a21fcbd with the same BusyBox-shaped PATH shim ps (usage on stderr, exit 1). QA1 confirmed real BusyBox behaves this way in an alpine container last round.
   - Live sleep process: isPidAlive gives null, and roleClaimWarning PRINTS the NOTE.
   - The same process SIGKILLed and reaped: isPidAlive gives false, and the NOTE is suppressed. So the fix did not break the positive-gone case.
 - Falsification: QA1 swapped b49fbcf's role-claims.js into a clone at a21fcbd and ran launcher_test.js. The new test "a ps that cannot answer (BusyBox's own shape) must NOT be read as process gone for a genuinely running process" FAILS on the old code and passes on the fix.

2. branch_state and a real repository git refuses (MEDIUM): FIXED, and demonstrated fixed.
 - "no-repo" is now returned only when git exits 0 printing something other than "true", or exits non-zero with stderr containing "not a git repository". Every other failure is ("unknown", None).
 - QA1's repro, re-run at a21fcbd: GIT_TEST_ASSUME_DIFFERENT_OWNER=1 in a real clone gives ('unknown', None) and "(branch unknown)". It no longer claims "not a git repository".
 - A genuinely empty non-repo directory still gives ('no-repo', None).
 - Falsification: with b49fbcf's sprint_lifecycle.py swapped in, smoke_test.sh FAILS on the new assertion. It printed "No sprints yet in ... (not a git repository)" for the dubious-ownership repo, and passes on the fix.
 - Advisory, not a finding: the stderr match is English-only. Under a non-English git locale, a genuine non-repo would degrade to "(branch unknown)". That is the permitted wording for undeterminable cases and never a false specific claim, so Req 2 still holds. Setting LC_ALL=C (or LANG=C) in that subprocess's env would make the positive case locale-independent, which is worth doing in a later sprint if Windows attendees run localized git.

EVERYTHING FROM ROUND 1 STILL HOLDS AT a21fcbd.
 - Req 1/1a/1c:
   - The launcher records its own pid, which stays alive for the whole awaited session.
   - Suppression happens only on an exact === false; a missing, invalid or old-format pid gives null, so the NOTE fires.
   - There is no "nobody else is working here" wording anywhere.
 - 1b: the measurements (macOS kill/ESRCH, the zombie visible only via ps STAT, pty-close taking down launcher and child) are recorded next to the code, naming platform and shutdown path. Windows is explicitly named as unmeasured, and LiveQA's criteria re-confirm it live.
 - Req 2/2a:
   - An unborn branch is named via symbolic-ref; a detached HEAD gives unknown.
   - Every tree_description() call site gets the text; nothing is special-cased.
   - The stderr banner is untouched.
   - Printed text is asserted for no-repo, unborn (a real git init), named, detached and dubious-ownership.
 - Req 3: package.json is 0.2.12 against published 0.2.11 (npm view), and the CHANGELOG entry is present.
 - Diff confinement: role-claims.js, sprint_lifecycle.py, launcher_test.js, smoke_test.sh, package.json, CHANGELOG.md, plus docs/sprints bookkeeping. All on the allowed list.

REQ 4. QA1 ran both suites at a21fcbd in a clean clone. node scripts/launcher_test.js: ALL LAUNCHER TESTS PASSED, exit 0. bash scripts/smoke_test.sh: ALL SMOKE TESTS PASSED, exit 0. pyflakes is clean.

FOR LIVEQA, carried from round 1. On Windows, after the trash can or Terminate All, confirm claude itself is gone via Get-Process, not only the launcher. run-role.js's orphan guard is POSIX-only; if claude ever outlives the node launcher there, the recorded pid reads as gone and the NOTE would be wrongly suppressed while a session is live.
